gloss: sense of impermanence; feeling of transience

definitions.gloss: sense of impermanence; feeling of transience
definitions.explanation: an awareness or emotional sense that all things are fleeting and nothing lasts forever, a key concept in Japanese aesthetics and Buddhist philosophy

examples.japanese: ⟦{桜|さくら}→桜：02212_sakura⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{無常感|むじょうかん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。
examples.english: Looking at cherry blossoms, I feel a sense of impermanence.

examples.japanese: {平家物語|へいけものがたり}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{深|ふか}い→深い：01211_fukai⟧{無常感|むじょうかん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{漂|ただよ}っている→漂う：04356_tadayou⟧。
examples.english: A deep sense of impermanence pervades The Tale of the Heike.

examples.japanese: ⟦{戦争|せんそう}→戦争：01450_sensou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{経験|けいけん}→経験：01179_keiken⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{人生|じんせい}→人生：03355_jinsei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{無常感|むじょうかん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{語|かた}っていた→語る：01930_kataru⟧。
examples.english: My grandfather, who experienced the war, often spoke about the transience of life.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{無常|むじょう}→無常：13422_mujou⟧ (impermanence, a Buddhist concept) and ⟦{感|かん}→〜感：28578_kan⟧ (feeling, sense). Refers to the emotional or aesthetic awareness that all things in life are temporary. This concept is central to Japanese literature, art, and philosophy.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無常感|むじょうかん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧: to feel a sense of impermanence
- {無常感|むじょうかん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{漂|ただよ}う→漂う：04356_tadayou⟧: for a sense of impermanence to pervade
- ⟦{深|ふか}い→深い：01211_fukai⟧{無常感|むじょうかん}: a deep sense of transience

CULTURAL NOTE:
The Buddhist concept of ⟦{無常|むじょう}→無常：13422_mujou⟧ (impermanence) has profoundly influenced Japanese culture. The famous opening of {平家物語|へいけものがたり} — {祇園精舎|ぎおんしょうじゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鐘|かね}→鐘：02654_kane⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧、⟦{諸行無常|しょぎょうむじょう}→諸行無常：14481_shogyoumujou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{響|ひび}き→響き：00098_hibiki⟧あり — encapsulates this sentiment. Cherry blossoms, autumn leaves, and other seasonal imagery are traditionally appreciated as expressions of this transience.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{無常|むじょう}→無常：13422_mujou⟧: impermanence — the core Buddhist concept
- ⟦{諸行無常|しょぎょうむじょう}→諸行無常：14481_shogyoumujou⟧: all things are impermanent — the Buddhist teaching itself
- {儚|はかな}さ: ephemerality, fleeting nature — a more emotional, literary term
- ⟦{物|もの}の{哀|あわ}れ→物の哀れ：30312_mononoaware⟧: the pathos of things — a related aesthetic concept emphasizing sensitivity to beauty and sadness
